overview: orator is a maximal, open-source, commercially-licensable speech-grading system in Python that runs on Windows/CPU. It grades a spoken sample on delivery (pace, pauses, fillers, monotone, energy) and content (vocabulary richness, readability, weak/hedging words, repetitions/false-starts), and — its signature feature — flags "got-tripped-up" moments where a speaker hesitated and reached for a worse word, suggesting a stronger one. The architecture is decoupled in two ways that satisfy the build constraints: (1) ASR is a pluggable backend behind an interface, and ALL analysis/scoring operates on a canonical in-memory `Transcript` schema (words with start/end/confidence), so the analysis modules are unit-testable from a JSON fixture with no model download or network; (2) the word-choice "better word + tripped-up" pass uses the Anthropic Claude API (model `claude-opus-4-8`) but has a deterministic offline lexicon-based fallback implementing the identical interface and emitting the identical schema, so the whole pipeline runs offline. The default ASR is faster-whisper (MIT) with a verbatim/disfluency-priming prompt + word_timestamps; CrisperWhisper (CC-BY-NC) is an opt-in high-accuracy backend gated behind a non-commercial flag. Optional acoustic prosody (Parselmouth/librosa) adds monotone/energy/pause metrics that need no transcript. Output is a 0-100 weighted score with per-dimension breakdown plus an HTML+JSON report that highlights fillers and trip-up moments inline in the transcript. The key preserved research insight: standard Whisper/Google STT delete fillers by design, so a verbatim-tuned decode (or a transcript-free acoustic detector) is mandatory before any filler counting — orator handles this at the ASR-backend layer, keeping the analysis layer engine-agnostic.
asrRecommendation: DEFAULT (commercial, offline-capable): faster-whisper (MIT) as the recognizer, configured for verbatim/filler retention — word_timestamps=True (gives word.start/.end/.probability), condition_on_previous_text=False (stops cross-window "cleanup"), and a filler-laden initial_prompt ("Umm, uh, like, you know, I mean...") to prime verbatim style and prevent suppression of um/uh. This is the safe-license, CPU-capable, GPU-optional core and exposes per-word confidence natively (correcting the common belief it doesn't). OPT-IN HIGH-ACCURACY: CrisperWhisper (nyrahealth) as a pluggable backend — it is purpose-built to emit explicit [UM]/[UH] tokens with disfluency-robust timestamps and beats Whisper large-v3 on WER (6.66% vs 7.7%). HARD LICENSE FLAG: CrisperWhisper weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) — gate it behind an explicit `--allow-noncommercial` flag and a config warning; never use it as the shipped default in a paid product. SECONDARY/REAL-TIME (optional): Vosk (Apache-2.0) for streaming/embedded CPU-only word+conf+timestamps, and whisper-timestamped (AGPL-3.0 — flag for SaaS) only as an eval/benchmark backend for its detect_disfluencies=True [*] gap markers. VERBATIM-FILLERS STRATEGY (two complementary tracks, fused on a shared time axis): TRACK A (lexical, default): a verbatim transcript source (faster-whisper verbatim prompt, or CrisperWhisper) -> normalize confidence -> lexicon+rule match for fillers/hedges/repetitions, with pause-gating (a lexicon hit preceded by an above-threshold inter-word gap = high-confidence filler). TRACK B (acoustic, optional, transcript-free): OpenOPAF-style filled-pause detection via Parselmouth (prolonged syllables with minimal spectral contrast) and inter-word silent-gap detection — robust even when ASR strips a filler. Reconcile A and B by timestamp for a robust count. NEVER count fillers off vanilla Whisper/Google output; gate the pipeline on a verbatim engine and add a regression test that transcribes a known clip and asserts the fillers reappear.

features.name: Filler-word detection (um/uh/like/you know)
features.measures: Count, rate, and timeline of filled pauses and discourse-marker fillers
features.howToCompute: Lexicon+rule match over verbatim word-timestamped transcript; context-sensitive rules for like/so/well/right (POS/position/collocation); pause-gate each hit (gap before word > speaker_median+~0.3s = high-confidence). filler_rate = fillers/total_words*100; also fillers_per_minute

features.name: Acoustic filled-pause detection (transcript-free)
features.measures: Filled pauses detected from the waveform when ASR stripped them
features.howToCompute: Parselmouth/PRAAT: flag prolonged syllables with minimal spectral contrast over rolling 5s windows; reconcile with Track A by timestamp

features.name: Silent-hesitation / pause detection
features.measures: Count, duration, placement of silent pauses; long/awkward (mid-clause) pauses
features.howToCompute: Inter-word gap = word[i+1].start - word[i].end; classify micro(<0.2s)/normal(0.2-0.7s)/long(>0.7s); flag long pauses mid-clause (not at punctuation/sentence boundary). Per-speaker-normalized threshold

features.name: Pace / WPM and consistency
features.measures: Words per minute overall and over rolling windows; pace stability
features.howToCompute: WPM = total_words/(speaking_seconds/60). Rolling-window WPM time series; consistency = stdev of windowed WPM. Configurable ideal band default 130-160 (presets per type)

features.name: Repetitions & false-starts (text)
features.measures: Immediate word/phrase repeats, partial words, self-corrections
features.howToCompute: Repeated-token heuristic (token[i].lower()==token[i-1]; n-gram repeats); partial-word heuristic (token ends in hyphen or is non-dict prefix of next); revision/edit-term heuristic (no/sorry/I mean as interregnum)

features.name: Vocabulary richness (length-robust)
features.howToCompute: Primary MATTR (window=50) and MTLD via lexicalrichness; report TTR only for fixed-length context. Do NOT use raw TTR as an absolute cross-length score

features.name: Weak / hedging / intensifier word detection
features.measures: Vague qualifiers, hedges, weasel words, overused boosters
features.howToCompute: Merged tagged lexicon (filler|hedge|weasel|intensifier) + rule linter (proselint/write-good/retext-style offline rules); hedge_density, intensifier_density per total_words

features.name: Got-tripped-up / word-finding moments
features.measures: Per-moment events where the speaker hesitated and reached for a worse word
features.howToCompute: FUSION: event_score = w1*hedge_flag + w2*vague_flag + w3*pause_norm + w4*(1-asr_word_confidence) + w5*filled_pause + w6*repair_span. Rank moments; per-speaker pause normalization. Lexical flag alone is NOT sufficient — must co-occur with pause/low-conf/repair

features.name: Better-word suggestion
features.measures: A stronger replacement for a flagged weak/vague word
features.howToCompute: OFFLINE: phrase->replacement dict + WordNet synonyms ranked by concreteness(Brysbaert)/specificity(SUBTLEX freq). LLM: Claude API (claude-opus-4-8) via client.messages.parse() into a Pydantic WordChoiceFinding list (output_format=); deterministic offline fallback emits same schema

features.name: Readability / sentence complexity
features.howToCompute: textstat: Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade, Gunning Fog, SMOG. Treat absolute grade cautiously (formulas built for prose); use change-over-sessions as the signal

features.name: Monotone / pitch variation
features.howToCompute: Parselmouth to_pitch() voiced frames; convert Hz->semitones (12*log2(f0/ref)); monotone = stdev(f0_semitones) or pitch range p95-p5; energy-weight F0 by intensity to ignore breathy frames

features.name: Loudness / energy dynamics
features.howToCompute: librosa RMS or Parselmouth intensity; flatness = std(RMS)/mean(RMS); range p95-p5 dB; composite flat-delivery flag = low F0_CV AND low energy_dynamics

features.name: Articulation rate vs speech rate
features.measures: Rushing inside fluent stretches vs over-pausing
features.howToCompute: Speech rate = syllables/total_time; Articulation rate = syllables/phonation_time (pauses excluded). Syllable nuclei via de Jong-Wempe Praat script (no transcript needed). balance = speaking/total

features.name: Voice quality (jitter/shimmer/HNR)
features.howToCompute: Parselmouth PointProcess + to_harmonicity; elevated jitter/shimmer + low HNR -> strained-voice flag

features.name: Composite confidence/fluency index
features.howToCompute: z-score and weight-blend fillers + hesitation pauses + hedging + repetitions into ONE fluency/confidence index rather than penalizing four times; show timestamped evidence per score

features.name: Eye contact / gesture / posture (video, opt-in tier)
features.howToCompute: MediaPipe (Apache-2.0) pose/face mesh + L2CS-Net (MIT) gaze; gate behind explicit opt-in + on-device. Avoid OpenFace (academic-only) and YOLO (AGPL) in commercial builds

dataSchemas.name: Word
dataSchemas.description: One recognized token with timing and confidence — the atomic unit all analysis consumes. Loadable from a JSON fixture so analysis is testable without ASR.
fields: text: str — surface form of the token (verbatim, fillers retained)
start: float — start time in seconds
end: float — end time in seconds
confidence: float | None — per-word confidence 0-1 (normalized across engines; None if unavailable)
is_filled_pause: bool — True if engine emitted an explicit filler token (e.g. CrisperWhisper [UM]); default False
normalized: str — lowercased/punct-stripped form for lexicon matching (derived)

dataSchemas.name: Transcript
dataSchemas.description: Canonical in-memory representation of one speech sample. Carries the full word list plus derived sentence/segment groupings and audio metadata. The single contract every analysis module depends on.
fields: words: list[Word] — ordered words for the whole sample
audio_path: str | None — path to source audio if available (enables acoustic track); None for fixtures
sample_rate: int | None — audio sample rate if known
duration_sec: float — total sample duration
speaking_sec: float — total phonation time (sum of word spans / VAD speech), pauses excluded
language: str — ISO code, default 'en'
engine: str — ASR backend id that produced this ('faster-whisper'|'crisper-whisper'|'vosk'|'fixture')
speaker_median_gap: float — median inter-word gap, for per-speaker pause normalization (derived)
sentences: list[tuple[int,int]] — (start_word_idx, end_word_idx) spans for sentence/clause grouping (derived)

dataSchemas.name: Finding
dataSchemas.description: One flagged item from any analysis module — a filler, a hedge, a repetition, or a tripped-up moment. Uniform shape so the report renderer and scorer treat all modules identically.
fields: kind: str — 'filler'|'hedge'|'weasel'|'intensifier'|'repetition'|'false_start'|'long_pause'|'tripped_up'|'weak_word'
word_index: int — index into Transcript.words (or first word of a span)
span: tuple[int,int] — (start_word_idx, end_word_idx) inclusive for multi-word findings
start: float — start time seconds (for timeline/highlight)
end: float — end time seconds
original: str — the offending text
suggestion: str | None — stronger replacement if applicable
rationale: str — human-readable why-flagged (for report + coaching)
score: float — confidence/severity of this finding 0-1
source: str — 'lexicon'|'rule'|'acoustic'|'llm' (provenance, esp. for tripped_up fusion)

dataSchemas.name: DimensionScore
dataSchemas.description: Score for one rubric dimension with its evidence, produced by the scorer.
fields: dimension: str — e.g. 'fillers'|'pace'|'pauses'|'vocabulary'|'word_choice'|'readability'|'prosody'
raw: float — raw metric value (e.g. filler_rate, WPM)
band: str — 'excellent'|'good'|'fair'|'poor'
points: float — 0-100 sub-score for this dimension
weight: float — weight in the composite (post-redistribution if a dimension was disabled)
findings: list[Finding] — supporting evidence (timestamped)
detail: dict — metric-specific extras (e.g. {'wpm':142,'consistency':18})

dataSchemas.name: Report
dataSchemas.description: Top-level graded result. Serializes to JSON and drives the HTML renderer. Contains the composite score, per-dimension breakdown, all findings, and enough to render the inline-highlighted transcript.
fields: overall_score: float — weighted 0-100
dimensions: list[DimensionScore] — per-dimension breakdown
findings: list[Finding] — all findings across modules, time-sorted
transcript: Transcript — the analyzed transcript (for inline highlighting)
metrics: dict — flat metric bag (filler_rate, wpm, mattr, mtld, flesch_kincaid, hedge_density, pause_count, etc.)
metadata: dict — engine, word-choice mode ('claude-opus-4-8'|'offline-lexicon'), config, version, timestamps
summary: str — short natural-language coaching summary

dataSchemas.name: WordChoiceFinding
dataSchemas.description: Pydantic model shared by BOTH the Claude API word-choice pass and the offline lexicon fallback, so they are interchangeable. Used as the output_format= for client.messages.parse(); schema obeys structured-output limits (additionalProperties:false, no numeric/string constraints, no recursion).
fields: word_index: int — index into Transcript.words
issue_type: str — 'weak'|'hedge'|'filler'|'tripped_up' (enum)
original: str — flagged text
suggestion: str | None — stronger word/phrase
rationale: str — why it is weak and why the suggestion is stronger
confidence: float — 0-1

modules.responsibility: WordChoiceAnalyzer interface + dispatcher that tries the LLM analyzer then falls back to the offline analyzer, guaranteeing identical WordChoiceFinding schema.
publicFunctions: analyze_word_choice(t: Transcript, cfg: Config) -> list[WordChoiceFinding] — online-then-offline dispatch
class WordChoiceAnalyzer(ABC) — analyze(t)->list[WordChoiceFinding]

modules.responsibility: Claude API word-choice analyzer. Uses client.messages.parse(model='claude-opus-4-8', output_format=WordChoiceFindingList Pydantic model) reading response.parsed_output; thinking={'type':'adaptive'}; output_config={'effort': cfg.llm_effort}. NO assistant prefill (400 on Opus 4.8) and NO citations (incompatible with structured outputs). Raises on any error so dispatcher falls back.
publicFunctions: class LLMWordChoice(WordChoiceAnalyzer) — analyze(t)->list[WordChoiceFinding]; build_user_message(t)->str (user-turn only; constraints go in the system prompt, not a prefill)

modules.responsibility: Deterministic offline word-choice + tripped-up detector. Fusion scoring (hedge/vague/pause/low-conf/filled-pause/repair); suggestions via REPLACEMENTS + WordNet ranked by concreteness/frequency. No network/model. This is the source of record for counts; the LLM pass is enrichment only.
publicFunctions: class OfflineWordChoice(WordChoiceAnalyzer) — analyze(t)->list[WordChoiceFinding]
detect_tripped_up(t: Transcript, findings: list[Finding], weights: dict) -> list[Finding] — fusion event scoring
rank_replacement(word:str)->str|None — WordNet synonyms ranked by Brysbaert concreteness / SUBTLEX freq

modules.responsibility: Loads Brysbaert concreteness + SUBTLEX frequency CSV norm tables; lookup for replacement ranking. Bundled CSVs so offline.
publicFunctions: concreteness(word:str)->float|None
frequency(word:str)->float|None
specificity_gain(orig:str, cand:str)->float

modules.responsibility: Construct-driven 0-100 composite: each module produces a DimensionScore; weights + bands applied; blends fillers/pauses/hedging/repetitions into one fluency index to avoid double-counting; when prosody is None (acoustic disabled) its weight is redistributed proportionally across the remaining dimensions.
publicFunctions: score(t: Transcript, all_findings: list[Finding], dim_scores: list[DimensionScore], cfg: Config) -> Report — applies rubric weights + bands -> overall_score + Report; redistributes weight of any absent DimensionScore

modules.responsibility: Render Report -> JSON and self-contained HTML with the transcript inline-highlighted (fillers, hedges, trip-up moments color-coded, hover rationale), per-dimension radar/bars, and timeline.
publicFunctions: render_html(report: Report, out_path: str) -> None
render_json(report: Report, out_path: str) -> None
highlight_transcript_html(report: Report) -> str — inline span-wrapped transcript

modules.responsibility: Orchestrates end-to-end: (transcribe OR load fixture) -> derive fields -> run analysis modules -> word-choice dispatch -> prosody (optional) -> scorer -> report. Pure wiring; each step swappable.
publicFunctions: run_pipeline(input_path: str, cfg: Config) -> Report — full run
run_on_transcript(t: Transcript, cfg: Config) -> Report — analysis-only path (no ASR), used by tests

modules.responsibility: argparse CLI: `orator grade <audio|transcript.json> [--offline] [--backend faster-whisper] [--allow-noncommercial] [--effort high] [--html out.html] [--json out.json]`. Picks ASR backend, builds Config, calls pipeline, writes report.
publicFunctions: main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int

pipeline: Input resolution: CLI receives either an audio file or a canonical Transcript JSON. If JSON, load via schema.load_transcript_json and SKIP ASR entirely (this is the offline/test path).

ASR (audio only): select backend from Config (default faster-whisper, MIT). Transcribe with verbatim settings (word_timestamps=True, condition_on_previous_text=False, filler initial_prompt). CrisperWhisper only if allow_noncommercial. Produce a Transcript with per-word start/end/confidence.
Derive: schema.derive_transcript_fields fills normalized forms, speaker_median_gap, sentence/clause spans, speaking_sec — everything downstream needs.
Lexical analysis (no model/network): run fillers, pauses, pace, repetitions, weak_words, vocabulary, readability modules -> Findings + DimensionScores.

Acoustic track (optional, audio + enable_acoustic): prosody module adds monotone/energy/articulation-rate + transcript-free acoustic filled-pause Findings; reconcile acoustic fillers with lexical fillers on the time axis. Returns (None, []) cleanly if no audio so the scorer can redistribute its weight.

Word-choice + tripped-up: wordchoice.base.analyze_word_choice tries LLMWordChoice (claude-opus-4-8 via messages.parse, output_format=Pydantic model, adaptive thinking, effort from config, no prefill); on any failure or use_llm=False, falls back to OfflineWordChoice (deterministic fusion + WordNet/concreteness suggestions). Both emit identical WordChoiceFinding lists -> mapped to Findings.

Fuse tripped-up moments: combine lexical hedge/weak flags + pause findings + low word.confidence + repair spans into ranked tripped_up Findings (offline.detect_tripped_up); per-speaker pause normalization.

Score: scorer applies the weighted rubric and bands, blending fillers/pauses/hedging/repetitions into one fluency/confidence sub-score to avoid quadruple-penalizing, redistributing the weight of any disabled dimension (e.g. prosody) proportionally across the rest, producing overall_score 0-100 + per-dimension breakdown.

Report: render_json writes the machine-readable Report; render_html writes a self-contained page with the transcript inline-highlighted (fillers, hedges, trip-up moments color-coded with hover rationale), a per-dimension breakdown, and a metric timeline.
Optional accomplishment logging: on a notable run, the wrapper appends an evidence-linked row to job-search/live/accomplishments-inbox.md (per workspace standing rule).

scoringRubric.bands: excellent <2/100 (Bortfeld baseline ~2.6); good 2-4; fair 4-6; poor >6 elevated, >10 distracting. Maps to 100/80/60/30 points.

scoringRubric.formula: WPM = words/(speaking_sec/60); penalty for deviation from band AND high windowed-WPM stdev
scoringRubric.bands: excellent within 130-160 (configurable; presets technical 130-140, persuasive 150-160) & consistent; fair 110-130 or 160-180; poor <110 or >180. Consistency stdev <15 full, >35 docked.

scoringRubric.formula: long_pause_rate = long_pauses/minutes; weight mid-clause (awkward) pauses more than boundary pauses
scoringRubric.bands: excellent few mid-clause long pauses + healthy phonation ratio; poor many >0.7s mid-clause pauses / very low balance ratio.

scoringRubric.formula: penalty from count & severity of tripped_up + weak_word findings; tripped_up weighted by event_score
scoringRubric.bands: excellent ~0 high-severity trip-ups; good a few low-severity; fair several; poor many high-severity (strong pause+low-conf+hedge co-occurrences).

scoringRubric.formula: MATTR (window 50) primary; MTLD secondary; map to richness band
scoringRubric.bands: excellent high MATTR/MTLD; poor low diversity / heavy crutch-word repetition. Length-robust — never raw TTR across lengths.
excellent low hedge+booster density; poor high density of 'I think/kind of/maybe' + 'very/really'.

scoringRubric.formula: Flesch-Kincaid grade + Flesch Reading Ease; used for relative tracking
scoringRubric.bands: scored gently/relatively — spoken language normally lower density; reward improvement over sessions, don't hard-penalize short clauses.

scoringRubric.formula: monotone = stdev(F0 semitones) energy-weighted; energy_dynamics = std(RMS)/mean(RMS); composite flat-delivery flag
scoringRubric.bands: excellent good pitch range + energy variation; poor low F0 stdev AND low energy dynamics (monotone+flat). If acoustic disabled, scorer redistributes this 0.12 weight proportionally across the other dimensions so the composite stays on a 0-100 scale.

dependencies: anthropic — Claude API client for the LLM word-choice pass (model claude-opus-4-8); structured output via client.messages.parse(output_format=WordChoiceFinding-list Pydantic model) reading response.parsed_output. Use thinking={'type':'adaptive'} and output_config={'effort': 'high'}; do NOT pass budget_tokens/temperature/top_p (400 on Opus 4.8), do NOT use assistant prefill (400 on Opus 4.8), do NOT enable citations (incompatible with structured outputs)
pydantic — typed Config + WordChoiceFinding schema validation + the structured-output model passed to messages.parse (additionalProperties false, enum issue_type, no numeric/string constraints)
faster-whisper — DEFAULT MIT ASR backend; verbatim decode with word_timestamps + per-word probability (CPU int8 / GPU float16)
transformers (nyrahealth crisper_whisper fork) — OPT-IN CrisperWhisper backend (CC-BY-NC; non-commercial gate)
torch — required by CrisperWhisper / any neural ASR or video backend; CPU build for Windows
vosk — OPTIONAL Apache-2.0 streaming CPU ASR backend (word/start/end/conf, embedded/real-time)
proselint — offline rule linter for weasel/hedging/redundancy flags (BSD-3, Python)
nltk — WordNet synonym expansion for offline better-word suggestions (permissive)
pandas — load Brysbaert concreteness + SUBTLEX frequency norm CSVs for replacement ranking
praat-parselmouth — OPTIONAL acoustic prosody: F0/intensity/jitter/shimmer/HNR + acoustic filled-pause detection (GPL-3.0 — isolate for distributed binaries; fine for internal/SaaS)
librosa — OPTIONAL acoustic I/O + RMS energy + pyin pitch (ISC, permissive)
numpy — numeric backbone for the acoustic track
mediapipe — OPTIONAL video tier: pose/face mesh (Apache-2.0) — only if visual grading enabled
l2cs-net — OPTIONAL video tier: gaze/eye-contact (MIT) — preferred over OpenFace (academic-only) and YOLO (AGPL)
risks: LICENSE TRAPS (commercial blocker): CrisperWhisper weights = CC-BY-NC 4.0; whisper-timestamped = AGPL-3.0; torchaudio MMS_FA align weights = CC-BY-NC; openSMILE/eGeMAPS = dual-license (not free for products); OpenFace = academic-only; YOLO = AGPL; amritkromana disfluency repo = no license (research-only). Mitigation: default to MIT/BSD/Apache/ISC stack (faster-whisper, librosa, Vosk, textstat, lexicalrichness, proselint, MediaPipe, L2CS-Net), gate NC/copyleft backends behind explicit flags, and note Parselmouth is GPL-3.0 (fine for SaaS, a consideration for shipped binaries).

Filler under-counting if ASR not verbatim: vanilla Whisper/Google strip um/uh by design. Mitigation: verbatim decode settings are mandatory at the backend; add a regression test that asserts known fillers reappear; offer the transcript-free acoustic track as a cross-check.

Confidence scores are NOT comparable across engines (Whisper logprob vs Vosk lattice vs alignment frame prob). Mitigation: normalize_confidence per engine before any thresholding in tripped-up fusion; Word.confidence is None-safe (the fusion term degrades gracefully when confidence is unavailable).
Raw TTR is length-confounded — using it as an absolute cross-length richness score is a correctness bug. Mitigation: MATTR/MTLD primary; TTR only at fixed length.
WPM 'ideal' band is context-dependent; hardcoding 111-140 is one tool's choice. Mitigation: configurable band defaulting ~130-160 with presentation-type presets, source cited in the rubric.
Over-counting like/so/well/right as fillers when used as legitimate content words. Mitigation: context-sensitive rules (POS/position/collocation), not raw substring match.

Double-counting low-confidence: fillers, hesitation pauses, hedging, repetitions all proxy the same thing. Mitigation: blend into one fluency/confidence index in the scorer; always show timestamped evidence next to each score.

Claude API drift / wrong call shape on Opus 4.8: budget_tokens, temperature, top_p, and last-assistant-turn prefills all 400; citations are incompatible with structured outputs. Mitigation: the LLM analyzer uses client.messages.parse with output_format= (a Pydantic model) + thinking={'type':'adaptive'} + output_config={'effort':...}, no prefill, no sampling params, no citations; constraints go in the system prompt; first call with a new schema pays a one-time compilation cost (24h cached). The deterministic offline lexicon fallback is the source of record for counts; the LLM is enrichment only, so any API error/non-determinism cannot corrupt the score.

Acoustic track fragility on Windows: numba/numpy version conflicts across librosa + parselmouth; my-voice-analysis/myprosody are unmaintained. Mitigation: pin environment, vendor only the de Jong-Wempe .praat script and call via Parselmouth rather than depending on the stale wrappers; acoustic track is optional and degrades gracefully (prosody returns None and the scorer redistributes its weight).

Per-speaker pause threshold: a global constant misfires across mics/rooms/speakers. Mitigation: normalize pause cutoff to speaker_median_gap + k; calibrate fusion weights (w1..w6) and k against a small human-annotated set of real stumbles.

Large-model download / offline requirement: ASR models are big and CrisperWhisper/Torch are heavy. Mitigation: analysis layer is fully decoupled and testable from a JSON Transcript fixture; ASR is pluggable; CI runs the offline path with no model download or network.
